items.title: Oracle Pulls Out of $7 Billion Tencent AI Agreement After US Pushback
bullets: Oracle has terminated a significant $7 billion AI-related agreement with Tencent, signaling a major escalation in the impact of U.S. regulatory pressure on cross-border technology partnerships.

This withdrawal highlights the growing difficulty for U.S. tech firms to maintain collaborative AI infrastructure projects with Chinese counterparts amid intensifying geopolitical scrutiny and export control enforcement.
items.reason: Direct material impact on major tech infrastructure and cross-border capital flows.

items.title: Voters Rejected A.I. in the Midterms. Now Comes an Era of Scrutiny.
bullets: The U.S. midterm elections saw voters reject data center projects in 40 out of 41 local ballot initiatives, indicating a significant political headwind for the physical infrastructure required to scale AI.

The shift toward a more regulatory-focused Democratic leadership suggests that the 'race against China' narrative is losing its efficacy as a justification for bypassing local environmental and community concerns.
items.reason: Signals a major shift in domestic policy and infrastructure development constraints for the AI sector.

items.title: Weebit Nano Launches Weebit Matrix In-Memory Compute Research Program
bullets: Weebit Nano has introduced a ReRAM-based hardware development kit designed to accelerate the prototyping of in-memory computing (IMC) architectures, which aim to process AI workloads directly within memory arrays.

Internal benchmarking suggests that this IMC approach could reduce inference power consumption by approximately 80x and latency by nearly 100x compared to traditional GPU-based implementations, signaling a potential shift in hardware efficiency for edge AI.
items.reason: Significant potential for hardware efficiency gains in AI inference.

items.title: OmniQ Platform Verifies 59 Quantum Papers For AI Scientists
bullets: The OmniQ platform has successfully converted 59 quantum research papers into executable workflows, revealing that current AI models struggle to reproduce scientific results due to communication gaps between human researchers and autonomous agents.

The development of 'Residual Agents' (RA) has demonstrated a significant performance boost, improving model accuracy from 68% to 85% while reducing computational costs by two-thirds, suggesting a scalable path toward autonomous scientific discovery.
items.reason: Breakthrough in AI-driven scientific research efficiency and reproducibility.

items.title: Alibaba and Tencent Face Stunning Nvidia Chip Shortfall Despite Millions of Orders
bullets: Major Chinese AI developers, including Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance, have collectively placed orders for approximately 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips to fuel their cloud and AI infrastructure expansion.
Current supply constraints suggest these firms may receive only tens of thousands of units over the next four months, representing a fulfillment rate of roughly 1% of total demand.
items.reason: Significant supply-demand imbalance impacting major international tech giants.

items.title: Nvidia Vera CPU: 1.8x Claim vs AMD’s 2.24x Rebuttal [2026]
bullets: Nvidia's Vera CPU and Vera Rubin NVL72 systems have officially reached general availability on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, marking a critical transition from roadmap slides to commercial production.

The competitive landscape is intensifying as AMD challenges Nvidia's performance claims, citing internal tests that show its EPYC Venice processors delivering 2.24x the platform-level performance of Vera-based systems.
items.reason: Direct competitive performance benchmarking between industry leaders in the critical data center CPU market.

items.title: EV Sales Crashed 41% In January—But These Brands Still Grew
bullets: U.S. electric vehicle registrations plummeted 41% in January compared to the prior year, causing the EV market share to contract significantly from 8.3% to 5.1%.
The decline follows the expiration of federal tax credits on September 30, 2025, prompting several major automakers to cancel planned EV models and scale back investments in the segment.
items.reason: Significant market contraction in the U.S. following policy shifts.

items.title: Tesla Finally Breaks Its 13-Month Sales Losing Streak in Europe
bullets: Tesla successfully reversed a 13-month sales decline in Europe, recording a 29.1% year-over-year increase in registrations with 13,740 units sold across the EU, UK, and EFTA regions.

Despite this recovery, the company faces intensifying competition from BYD, which saw a 185.3% year-over-year surge in European registrations, highlighting the aggressive expansion of Chinese manufacturers in the region.
items.reason: Key recovery for a major market player amid rising competition.

items.title: Voters rebuff data centers in every ballot measure except one during the 2026 midterms
bullets: Voters rejected 40 out of 41 local ballot measures aimed at restricting data center construction, signaling a significant political headwind for the industry's expansion plans in key states like Ohio.

The election of new Democratic governors in states like Ohio and Texas, who campaigned on stricter data center regulation and utility cost-sharing, creates material regulatory risk for multi-billion dollar infrastructure projects.
items.reason: Widespread political backlash threatens the viability of massive AI infrastructure pipelines.

items.title: Big Four Hyperscalers Seek $131 Billion for AI Infrastructure
items.source: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
bullets: Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Oracle are aggressively raising $131 billion in capital through loans and bond offerings to sustain their massive AI infrastructure buildout despite rising regulatory and construction hurdles.

Amazon alone is securing up to $80 billion in vendor financing for technology infrastructure, while Microsoft is issuing $25 billion in corporate bonds, highlighting the immense capital intensity required to maintain current AI capacity growth.
items.reason: Massive capital mobilization underscores the scale of AI infrastructure spending despite political headwinds.

items.title: Artemis II left temporary holes in Earth’s upper atmosphere that could have affected GPS, new study finds
bullets: A study published in Geophysical Research Letters reveals that the Artemis II mission created significant ionospheric disturbances, with effects ten times more intense than those observed from SpaceX Starship test flights.

These atmospheric gaps, stretching over 3,100 miles, caused localized GPS positioning errors, raising concerns about the long-term impact of increased lunar and interplanetary launch cadences on global navigation infrastructure.
items.reason: Operational risks to critical global navigation infrastructure.

items.title: Strengthening India’s Space Sovereignty
bullets: India's space economy has reached a valuation of USD 9 billion, with projections estimating growth to USD 40–45 billion over the next decade as the sector shifts toward private-led commercialization.

Private investment in the Indian space sector has surged to over USD 618 million by March 2026, supported by 113 government authorizations granted to 52 non-government entities for satellite and launch operations.
items.reason: Significant growth and private capital influx in a major emerging space market.

items.title: After the US midterms, what will a lame duck Trump mean for the global economy?
bullets: The loss of Republican control in both the House and Senate creates a 'lame duck' presidency, signaling a period of political volatility that investors fear will exacerbate uncertainty in financial markets.

While markets initially rallied on the prospect of checks and balances, the potential for a more aggressive foreign policy and 'Mr. Veto' domestic obstructionism poses significant risks to global growth and inflation stability.
items.reason: Significant geopolitical and domestic policy shift impacting global markets.

items.title: Global central banks hit pause in October after September hiking spree
bullets: Major monetary authorities, including the Federal Reserve and ECB, paused rate hikes in October following a aggressive September, reflecting a cautious approach to persistent inflationary pressures.

Despite the pause, economists warn that the tightening cycle is not necessarily over, as rising energy costs and supply chain disruptions linked to the Iran conflict continue to threaten price stability.
items.reason: Broad shift in global monetary policy stance affecting asset valuations.

items.title: Global Central Banks Are Buying Gold. Russia Is Selling More Than Anyone to Cover Its Budget Deficit
bullets: Russia has sold 18.66 metric tons of gold in Q3 2026 to finance a record wartime budget deficit, marking the largest drawdown of reserves since the 1998 financial crisis.
While Russia liquidates assets to cover a $270.8 billion cumulative war deficit, global central banks are moving in the opposite direction, increasing gold purchases by 42% year-over-year.
items.reason: Significant divergence in central bank reserve management and Russian fiscal distress.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher after Democrats win Congress; data center stocks tumble
bullets: The U.S. equity market experienced a significant rally following the Democratic victory in Congressional elections, marking the largest post-midterm surge in 44 years.

While the broader market trended upward, the data center sector faced notable selling pressure, reflecting investor rotation or specific concerns regarding the policy implications of the new legislative landscape.
items.reason: Major political shift impacting broad market sentiment and sector-specific performance.

items.title: Figma sinks after earnings beat as company prioritizes long-term growth with AI changes
bullets: Figma shares fell 7% despite beating expectations with $391.4 million in revenue and 10 cents adjusted EPS, as investors reacted to the company's strategic pivot toward long-term AI-driven growth.

Management raised full-year operating margin guidance to 11% and revenue projections to approximately $1.498 billion, signaling confidence in durable growth despite a planned deceleration in Q4 revenue expansion to 33%.
items.reason: Significant market reaction to earnings and strategic shift in a high-growth tech company.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield slides as traders mull over Democrats' midterm victories, oil prices drop
bullets: The 10-year Treasury yield fell by over 6 basis points to 4.884%, while the 30-year and 2-year notes saw declines of 5 and 4 basis points respectively.

Market participants are interpreting the Democratic sweep of Congress as a potential catalyst for reduced deficit spending, which could improve the long-term fiscal outlook and dampen inflationary pressures.
items.reason: Direct market impact of election results on benchmark yields.

items.title: AI debt binge isn't crowding out Treasuries, TBAC says
bullets: The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee concluded that record corporate issuance for AI investment is not crowding out demand for Treasuries, attributing recent yield volatility to growth and policy expectations instead.

The committee noted that while heavy tech-sector borrowing has widened credit spreads, the broader investor base, including pension funds and households, remains capable of absorbing current Treasury supply.
items.reason: Institutional analysis of structural bond market dynamics.

items.title: Chinese exports of rare earth to Japan crater after PM's Taiwan remark
bullets: Chinese exports of yttrium to Japan plummeted 98% year-on-year between January and September 2026, following diplomatic tensions sparked by Japanese political remarks regarding Taiwan.

As China controls the vast majority of the global yttrium market, this supply restriction creates significant downstream risks for manufacturers of semiconductors, jet engines, and medical equipment relying on these critical materials.
items.reason: Significant supply chain disruption for critical industrial materials.

items.title: Canada, China Extend Tariff Deal, Aim to Boost Canadian Exports
bullets: Canada and China have extended their bilateral trade agreement through late 2028, providing a rare window of stability for agricultural and commodity exporters amidst broader global protectionist trends.

The extension signals a strategic effort to maintain market access for Canadian goods, directly impacting agricultural market valuations and supply chain planning for firms operating between the two nations.
items.reason: Important trade policy development affecting commodity market stability.

items.title: Beijing, HK boost investment ties
bullets: Beijing and Hong Kong-based companies signed 47 agreements valued at approximately $7.48 billion, focusing on high-growth sectors including biopharmaceuticals, commercial aerospace, and technological services.

The symposium highlighted Hong Kong's role as the primary source of overseas capital for Beijing, with cumulative investment exceeding $150 billion, reinforcing the city's strategic function as a 'super connector' for mainland firms expanding globally.
items.reason: Significant cross-border capital flow and strategic economic integration.

items.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong to be sentenced for collusion
bullets: Joshua Wong faces sentencing for 'foreign collusion' under the national security law, with potential penalties ranging from 10 years to life imprisonment if the court deems the offense of a 'grave nature'.

This high-profile case underscores the ongoing legal and political risks within the jurisdiction, as authorities utilize national security legislation to address lobbying activities and international sanctions advocacy.
items.reason: High-profile legal developments impacting the city's political and regulatory environment.
